basis: Chronic mesenteric vascular insufficiency causes intestinal ischemia; both intestinal and vascular disease define the concept.
Cardiac conduction disorder defined by short PR interval and atrial tachyarrhythmias.
Pyogenic infection of the bile ducts; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Predominantly gonadal reproductive malignancy; rare pineal origins do not represent the group. Metastatic sites are variable and lack qualifying frequency evidence.
Inborn bile acid conjugation defect; hepatic injury supported by elevated transaminases in 3/7 and jaundice in 7/7. Secondary rickets in 2/7 excluded.
Intestinal infection produces neurotoxin that disables neuromuscular junctions. Weakness, diplopia and respiratory failure reflect neural dysfunction, not separate organ damage.
Inherited ocular refractive and growth disorder; high myopia in 7/8 and increased globe axial length in 3/3.
Infantile immune-mediated ulcerative colitis. Anemia and motor delay in one reported patient do not establish direct blood or neurologic damage.
Inherited retinal degeneration; rod-cone dystrophy in 18/18, reduced visual acuity in 17/18 and visual field constriction in 14/16.
Glycosylation disorder; hepatic injury with AST elevation in 8/8 and coagulation dysfunction with factor XI reduction in 6/6. Other organs have isolated reports without reliable group frequencies.
